A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LMEE-Bench and MemoryExplorer. All 21 pages of each version, including supplementary Sections 7–15, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LMEE-Bench and GOAT-Bench evaluations, ablations, full-set results and physical-robot demonstrations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, supplementary ablations and real-world demonstrations.

M1.justification: The memory retrieval procedure, GRPO fine-tuning, multi-task reward and inference outputs remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the supplementary training and inference prompts are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HM3DSem-derived LMEE tasks, GOAT-Bench and office robot scenarios. MP3D-EQA is added only to the contextual benchmark overview in Table 1, without reported training or evaluation on it.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in Tables 2, 3 and 5, including Explore-EQA, 3D-Mem, RA-Mem and the retrieval-augmented QA models. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The 58-task LMEE subset, 166-task full test set, GOAT-Bench subset, metrics and training settings are unchanged. The navigation success criterion is reworded but retains the same one-meter threshold.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the question-type, training-task, reward and hyperparameter ablations in Tables 4 and 6–8. The question-type analysis, robot demonstrations, complete-task example and failure cases are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The same point estimates and training curves are reported. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Experimental values and qualitative outcomes are unchanged throughout the main text and supplement. For example, MemoryExplorer retains SR/SPL of 23.53/14.99 on the LMEE subset, 22.05/14.26 on the full set and 46.40/28.03 on the GOAT-Bench subset.

T1.justification: The formal task definition, memory similarity and retrieval definitions, training objective and reward equations remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about LMEE, its benchmark and reinforcement learning for active memory retrieval. Small wording edits do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of memory retrieval benefits, failure analyses in Sections 10–11 and limitations in Section 15 are unchanged. The revised Figure 4 discussion paraphrases the same example without introducing a substantive interpretation or qualification.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, training time, hyperparameters and prompts are unchanged. V2 prints the project URL explicitly, but v1 already links to that same address; both describe code and data release as forthcoming.

R1.justification: V2 adds eleven references, revises citation groups in Sections 1–2 and includes MP3D-EQA in Table 1. These expand background coverage without substantially changing the positioning around active versus passive memory use.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited sentence edits in the metrics, qualitative discussion and conclusion, adds corresponding-author identification and introduces funding acknowledgments. The overall organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a benchmark row, figure spacing and text flow are adjusted, and page-number footers are removed. The abstract and conclusion no longer spill onto subsequent pages; experimental displays and supplementary layouts otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark context and small editorial adjustments provide limited polish. The method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations—including the complete supplement—remain unchanged, so the revision does not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
